task_specification.objective: Make Mournlight closure-ready by preserving a truthful 32-enemy representative workload across three profile cycles, isolating ordinary victory presentation ownership from diagnostic fixtures, and completing the natural seven-to-ten-minute release route with viable build, result, credits, and replay transactions while preserving all accepted authored assets and lifecycle baselines.

diagnosis.root_cause: Release convergence is blocked by three separable causes: the representative profile permits combat attrition to reduce its third sample from 32 to 31 enemies; ordinary-route victory has not proven that the accepted Cheer binding retains terminal ownership through result and Retry; and the complete 420–600 second victory/build/credits/replay release transaction lacks candidate-bound qualification. The retained cemetery, Warden package, semantic mappings, 40-enemy pool, bounded neighbor work, and clean teardown are accepted baselines, not replacement targets.

stop_conditions: Stop if native project import or host boot regresses, or if normal play produces fatal or recurring runtime errors.
Stop any animation treatment that would alter the preserved Warden package hierarchy, seven accepted clip mappings, model transforms, lantern attachments, or authored source values.
Stop any density repair that suppresses legitimate combat deaths or rewards, enlarges the 40-enemy pool, removes authored role variants, or relaxes existing work and lifecycle caps.
Do not claim the 60 FPS target from llvmpipe; phase closure requires a fresh hardware-backed 1920x1080 profile with renderer identity.
Do not edit or disposition the deferred cracked-bell landmark issue or expand into mandatory backlog contracts during this iteration.
Stop after the three selected gaps are implementation-ready for Tester recapture; formal issue and phase closure remain Tester and host responsibilities.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different root-cause strategy from repeated transform or mapping treatments: retain the accepted animation profile and isolate terminal presentation ownership across victory, result, and Retry; separate diagnostic workload maintenance from ordinary combat so deaths remain causal while the sampled cohort is replenished deterministically; then qualify the untouched natural route as a complete release transaction rather than substituting diagnostic jumps.

code: Run the frozen native project and host boot checks; require clean import, launch, GDScript parsing, and no recurring runtime errors.
Inspect release configuration to confirm editor-only validation actions have no physical bindings and cannot enter release exports or qualify ordinary-route receipts.
Compare retained Warden mappings, package hierarchy, pool size, neighbor budget, presentation caps, manifests, and notices against their accepted candidate values.
runtime: Tester should capture an ordinary five-wave victory and Retry, binding Bellkeeper defeat, `victory`/`Cheer`, one result commit, visible result, and reset to `idle`/`Idle` without diagnostic preparation.

Tester should run three identical 1920x1080 prepare/advance/reset profile cycles, verify 32-enemy minimum/start/end workload and clean isolation, then repeat frame-time qualification on the designated hardware renderer with adapter identity.
Tester should play failure and victory routes plus focused-bolt, sweep, and orbit builds; verify truthful results, Credits & Notices, Retry, Return to Title, and three stable restart baselines.

Patrol boot/title/play, movement/dash, automatic combat, enemy lifecycle, collection/draft, pause/resume, HUD truth, audio ownership, boss phases, result, and replay with black-box play and authoritative snapshots.
visual: Capture the same shipped high-angle camera at ordinary play and representative final-wave density; require readable silhouettes, escape lanes, warm-versus-cool hierarchy, bounded effects, and no new occlusion or placeholders.

Capture victory onset, result, Retry gameplay, and Credits at 1920x1080; require authored full-viewport composition, legible statistics/build summary, clear focus, and no clipped or debug-like presentation.
Use short-event onset, impact, and recovery frames for dash, weapons, hurt, boss warning/phase, death, and victory while confirming effects never conceal hostile telegraphs.

done_when: An ordinary, non-diagnostic Bellkeeper defeat changes the Warden to semantic `victory`, resolves the preserved `Cheer` clip on the 41-bone authored deformation owner, and holds terminal ownership through the visible victory/result handoff.
Ordinary Retry clears terminal ownership and returns the same preserved binding to semantic `idle` with resolved clip `Idle`, without stale animation, audio, pause, or process ownership.
Idle, move, dash, cast, hurt, death, and victory remain seven distinct exact authored mappings; missing or unrelated fallback clips fail closed and no wrapper transform animation is introduced.

Victory, death, boss warning/phase, player hurt, upgrade selection, weapon, pickup, and result audio remain event-owned, bounded, and separately observable, with no duplicated voice, leaked loop, hum, unexpected speech, or generic generated tone after result, Retry, or Title.
Dense gameplay preserves the accepted moonlight/lantern hierarchy, bounded hostile and friendly VFX, readable telegraphs, and the retained staggered authored enemy animation mechanism.
tasks.instructions: Repair the terminal presentation boundary without remapping clips or tuning imported transforms. Give the preserved semantic binding an explicit victory/death lease that survives combat teardown and result presentation, while Retry or Title performs the sole reset to idle. Keep animation state driven by authoritative movement and combat events. Audit the directly coupled audio and effect owners so terminal and priority semantics remain bounded across dense play, pause, result, Retry, and Title. Expose truthful snapshots for semantic state, resolved clip, deformation owner, terminal lease, audio owner, and reset generation; do not create a diagnostic victory shortcut or treat a prepared result as ordinary-route evidence.
tasks.title: Isolate ordinary victory presentation ownership

done_when: Each editor-only prepare step resolves exactly 32 active ordinary enemies with the Bellkeeper, all three weapon families, production pickups, UI, animation, VFX, light, and audio owners present before sampling begins.

During each four-second sample, legitimate attacks, damage, deaths, and rewards remain enabled while a deterministic profile-only workload coordinator restores losses within the same authoritative lifecycle boundary and reports requested, minimum, start, end, and replenished counts.
Three consecutive prepare/advance/reset cycles each report a 32-enemy representative workload and the same bounded roster, seed, build, camera, viewport, work caps, and renderer receipt.
Every immediate and next-frame reset reports 0 live enemies, 40 pooled enemies, and zero boss, projectiles, pickups, effects, wisps, attack ledgers, registered neighbors, or audio voices.

The ordinary wave director is unchanged by diagnostic workload maintenance, and the preserved 40-enemy pool, 12-candidate neighbor budget, telegraph/light/audio caps, role variants, and staggered manual animation mechanism remain intact.
tasks.instructions: Fix the profile density drift at the workload-ownership boundary, not by making enemies immortal or loosening production caps. Add deterministic, editor-only cohort maintenance to the existing prepare/advance/reset transaction so a combat death completes normally, including reward causality, and a replacement is admitted immediately from the preserved pool while sampling is active. Record minimum and end workload plus replenishment receipts per cycle, and keep preparation stable and separate from advancement. Preserve existing teardown ordering and ordinary run behavior. Do not encode a renderer pass verdict in candidate code.
tasks.title: Hold the representative profile at truthful density

done_when: A fresh title-screen Play transaction completes all five authored waves and the two-phase Bellkeeper through ordinary input and runtime systems in 420–600 seconds, with no diagnostic jump and exactly one victory/result commit.

The ordinary route records composition escalation, an elite, natural Bellkeeper entry and defeat, truthful upgrade transactions, authoritative statistics, and a result containing time, level, defeated enemies, damage dealt, damage taken, selected upgrades, and outcome.
